UMPI YourPace vs UMass Global MyPath: business-degree costs and transfer

UMPI YourPace and UMass Global MyPath both offer competency-based business study, but they bill different periods and evaluate prior learning under different rules. Compare the requirements left after your own records are evaluated, then budget the paid sessions or billing periods needed to complete them.

Compare my remaining degree work

Compare exact programs rather than the school names

YourPace is the University of Maine at Presque Isle’s competency-based format. MyPath is the University of Massachusetts Global’s competency-based format. The comparison here concerns undergraduate business planning; a conventional term-based degree, another major or a different catalog at either university can have other rules.

UMPI is accredited by the New England Commission of Higher Education as part of the University of Maine System’s accreditation. UMass Global is institutionally accredited by the WASC Senior College and University Commission. Institutional accreditation and a university’s willingness to consider outside credit are separate from approval of a particular course for your exact degree. Also check your intended graduate program, employer or professional requirement.

Use the actual billing units and preserve the price discrepancy

UMPI’s current 2026–27 YourPace undergraduate tuition is $1,800 per eight-week session. UMass Global’s live tuition page lists MyPath bachelor’s tuition at $3,500 per 24-week billing period and $7,000 for a 48-week academic year, with a 12-unit minimum per billing period. That page is headed 2025–2026 and directs readers to the academic catalog for the latest comprehensive rates. The live table is a source-dated scenario, not confirmation of a 2026–27 rate. Nor is the unit minimum a promise of degree completion within one period.

A current UMass Global General Business MyPath BBA page still advertises $3,400 for six months of access. The two official pages disagree. This review did not establish when a price changed or which individual offer applies. Use $3,500 only as the published 2025–26 tuition-table scenario, obtain written confirmation before enrolling, and keep the displayed $3,400 claim visible as an unresolved source discrepancy.

Current published structures checked November 27, 2026; tuition scenarios before other applicable charges and financial aid.
FormatPublished billing structureIllustrative paid periods
UMPI undergraduate YourPace$1,800 per eight-week session, 2026–27One / two / three sessions: $1,800 / $3,600 / $5,400
UMass Global MyPath bachelor’s$3,500 per 24-week period on live tuition page headed 2025–2026One / two periods: $3,500 / $7,000; BBA page still displays $3,400; confirm applicable current rate

Neither set of examples forecasts completion. A 24-week billing period is not automatically six calendar months; use the university’s actual calendar and charges.

Separate overall transfer space from ACE and major requirements

For a 120-credit bachelor’s degree, a 30-credit institutional requirement leaves a mathematical maximum of 90 outside credits. It does not establish 90 ACE credits or 90 applicable credits for every student. UMPI’s FAQ describes no fixed transfer-in count while separately requiring 30 UMPI credits for a bachelor’s, including 12 in the major and nine of those at the upper level. The requirements that remain control the useful transfer total.

UMPI’s currently published credit-for-prior-learning page separately limits combined bachelor’s CPL, including ACE-recommended learning, to 30 credits; its linked 2025–26 handbook also states 30. That published source-specific limit is separate from 30-credit residency and the 90-credit overall outside ceiling. This review did not establish a new adoption date or a cohort-specific exception for particular approved provider courses.

UMass Global’s published 2025–26 undergraduate competency-based degree policy requires at least 30 equivalent credits in residence, including LBSC 320 and LBSC 321. The 2025–26 competency-based transfer policy evaluates eligible accredited-college work against credit-hour courses and then competencies, with B− or better required under that published policy. It also considers ACE-recommended learning subject to degree and residency requirements. These catalog excerpts were rechecked November 27, but their rules were not independently confirmed against the applicable 2026–27 catalog; obtain the current cohort-specific requirements before purchasing courses. This review did not establish a separate universal numerical MyPath ACE cap.

At either university, ask which exact requirements your college courses, exams and recommended learning fill. Confirm source-specific limits, minimum results, academic level, duplicate learning and the applicable catalog. A provider partnership page is useful evidence to investigate, but it is not a complete degree audit.

Do not buy courses based on an unverified future UMPI rule

This review did not find a primary-source announcement establishing the reported December 28 ACE-to-major transition or a grandfathering rule. A community report or an inaccessible catalog page cannot establish the effective date, affected program or treatment of existing students. Do not alter a historical completion or remove previously awarded credit based on that report.

Before starting a new ACE course for a required business subject, obtain the current placement and any cohort-specific conditions from UMPI. Keep the answer with your catalog and original completion record. Overall transfer space, a combined prior-learning limit and major residency are different checks; none should be substituted for another. A date-specific policy update belongs in the plan only after its scope and authority are clear.

Check the transcript and assessment experience you need

UMass Global’s published 2025–26 competency-based catalog describes a mastery transcript using M for mastery, without a conventional GPA, and a credit-hour conversion that can be requested under its stated procedure. Confirm the applicable current catalog and transcript policy. If you may later transfer again or apply to graduate study, ask the next institution how it evaluates that record. A conversion is not permission to invent traditional letter grades or assume a particular admission result.

Self-paced and competency-based do not establish a blanket non-proctored assessment policy. This review did not verify a universal proctor-free promise for either business route. Ask about the actual remaining courses, final assessments, written work, technical requirements and feedback process. Your comfortable assessment format and the time needed for evaluation belong in the comparison alongside tuition.

Make the evaluation and a realistic pace scenario decide

Request the same comparison from both universities: which existing credits apply, what named requirements remain, which work must be completed in residence, and what source restrictions apply to any proposed outside courses. Include the exact business specialization, delivery format, intended start and catalog. If a full course map is unavailable, keep the unresolved rows visible rather than filling them with a generic transfer percentage.

Then estimate paid periods using your available study time, prerequisites, grading and required final work. A hypothetical student taking two UMPI sessions would budget $3,600 in session tuition. A hypothetical student finishing within one MyPath period using the published 2025–26 tuition-table rate would budget $3,500. That $100 arithmetic difference does not identify the cheaper degree for you: the remaining coursework and actual number of paid periods can change it materially.

Add outside-course spending, any other applicable charges and your individual funding. Compare a slower scenario before committing to a subscription. These are sourced program comparisons, not complete DegreeSteps course templates for either business route; the universities determine the individual awards.

Bring the same course record to both comparisons

Keep your original college courses, certificates and completion dates together before requesting the two evaluations.

About this research

DegreeSteps editorial team · Degree planning and transfer-credit research

We explain educational choices using university catalogs, receiving-school course agreements, provider guidance, and the same researched degree models used by DegreeSteps. Our articles distinguish proposed coursework, original learning records, and individual university awards. Worked examples identify their program, format, units, and relevant dates. Founder stories are attributed as reported experience, without invented transcripts, savings totals, or reviewer credentials.
